voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: Forty-three thousand cars cross this bridge every day, on the Saw Mill River Parkway, just outside Yonkers. You've probably been one of them.

State inspectors rate its substructure 'Critical' — the worst score they give a bridge that's still open to traffic. It's also flagged 'scour critical': an open question about whether the river is eating away at what holds it up.
That rating has stood for more than five years. Nobody fixed it. Nobody replaced it. It's been left exactly as it was found.
A few exits north, on this same parkway, the state spent thirty-eight million dollars rebuilding two other bridges — finished in twenty twenty-three. This one wasn't part of that project.
beats.cap:
$38M.
TWO BRIDGES FIXED.
NOT THIS ONE.

beats.vo: It's not in any other funded plan either. No news story. No date to replace it. Just the record — and a bridge you've probably already driven, with no way to know.
beats.cap:
YOU HAD
NO WAY TO KNOW

facts.source: Verified via the bridge-story-engine two-tier pipeline (Sonnet-5-wide scout -> adversarial frontier verify, 0 false negatives across a 98-bridge calibrated batch). NBI ID NY-000000005500699, NY Route 987D over the Saw Mill River / Saw Mill River Parkway, Yonkers, southern Westchester County NY. Owner: NY State Highway Agency. Traffic 43,153 vehicles/day (2021 count). Substructure rated Critical (NYSDOT's worst routine condition rating); overall condition Poor for 5+ years. Flagged scour-critical, unresolved. State completed a separate $38M rebuild of two other Saw Mill River Parkway bridges in Pleasantville (Exits 26-28) in Jan 2023 -- this bridge was explicitly not part of that project. Also not in the $115M Lower Westchester Bridge Bundle or a 2025 $16.4M I-287-over-the-parkway joint job (different structure). No news coverage or programmed replacement located for this exact bridge.
facts.honesty_guard_followed: Critical substructure + scour-critical are framed throughout as advanced deferred deterioration and an open, unresolved foundation question -- never as collapse-imminent or unsafe-to-drive-today. No script line asserts or implies the bridge could fail or is dangerous right now. The dread is duration-of-neglect + heavy daily reliance + the documented contrast with the neighboring bridges that got fixed, not present-tense danger. No officials, dates, or specifics were invented beyond the verified facts above.
